# AI Contribution and Authorship Statement {.unnumbered}

This dissertation represents the intellectual work of Damian W. Betebenner
with substantive and continuous assistance from AI-based systems —
principally Anthropic's Claude models, operating through the dissertation.ai
onboarding platform and Claude Code development sessions — integrated into
every phase of the work: research design, software implementation,
registered analysis, and writing. The project is itself, by design, a study
in AI-native scholarship: it deliberately stress-tests the dataimago /
dissertation.ai infrastructure while developing the IRTc model family.

## Role of AI in the research and writing process {.unnumbered}

- **Theoretical development**: The IRTc research program (the founding
  conjecture, the model ladder, the work packages) was authored by the
  human researcher in a project charter; the AI executed and elaborated the
  ladder — the Level-1 product-copula wrapper with its exact-equivalence
  proof obligations, and the native Level-2 one-factor likelihood that
  replaced the wrapped engine after its scalability wall was documented.
- **Implementation**: The AI drafted the `irtc` R package test-first
  (simulators, baseline fits, copula fits, held-out evaluation), under a
  regime in which every capability claim is re-verified by the continuous
  integration test suite (~190 tests), including reproduction oracles
  against the reference engine at documented numerical tolerances.
- **Analysis**: All model comparisons ran as pre-registered experiments —
  registered in `experiments/registry.yaml` before execution, evaluated by
  frozen hash-gated scripts, recorded append-only — with a typed claim
  ledger (`research/literature/claims.yaml`) gating what may be asserted.
  The registered acceptance thresholds were set before any data were seen;
  where results fell short of them, no claims were made.
- **Expository and editorial support**: The AI drafted the knowledge-base
  wiki, the benchmark report (rendered entirely from committed run
  artifacts), and thesis scaffolding, under the writing specification
  committed at `writing/STYLE.md`.

## Scope and oversight {.unnumbered}

| Contribution area | AI role | Human oversight |
|---|---|---|
| Research program | executed and elaborated | authored the charter; adjudicates all direction |
| R package code | drafted test-first | CI oracles vs reference engines; R CMD check |
| Benchmark evidence | ran registered experiments | pre-registered gates; append-only registry; claim audit |
| Prose | drafted under `writing/STYLE.md` | maintainer review; no-unsupported-claims rule |

The verification discipline is structural rather than trust-based: claims
live in a typed ledger citing the tests that re-verify them; experiments
cannot produce evidence unless registered first; failure modes (a
boundary-probability evaluator bug, an engine scalability wall, a
convergence failure that voided an acceptance criterion) are documented in
the same public record as successes.

## Authorship and responsibility {.unnumbered}

Despite the substantive role of AI in this work, the author retains full
responsibility for all claims, formulations, and conclusions presented
herein. The AI systems are not listed as authors, consistent with
prevailing norms from the International Committee of Medical Journal
Editors (ICMJE) and leading scholarly publishers: they do not meet
authorship criteria concerning accountability, consent, or the capacity to
respond to review.
